newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.

text.p: For the week of Oct. 14, here are some of the top stories reported in major U.S. technology trade publications.

ELECTRONIC ENGINEERING TIMES - Modem makers are rushing to develop 56 kilobit transmission technology that roughly doubles the speed of Internet communications over standard telephone lines, but critics question the usefulness of a technology that remains rooted in older analog technology, while depending on digital signals at central switching sites, Electronic Engineering Times reported in its October 14 issue.

COMPUTER RESELLER NEWS - Microsoft Corp is in talks with its distributors on how to create a "level playing field" in the pricing it sets for various computer vendors, CRN reported in its October 14 issue. Pricing changes to be made on the Office 97 product would eliminate the substantial discount that direct PC makers Dell Computer Corp and Gateway 2000 Inc have enjoyed over rivals, it said.

Reflecting the imperative to cut costs, contract manufacturers of personal computers are designing an increasing share of the machines, raising concerns among computer distributors that PCs may become less differentiated and harder to sell as PC makers rely on similar designs, CRN also reported.

PC WEEK - Unisys Corp, Wyse Technology and International Business Machines Corp and others will introduce low-cost machines that meet the Network Computer standard, but few of the devices will come close to the $500 price originally mooted for the new class of machines, PC Week reported in its October 14 issue. For example, the Unisys machine, priced at about $1,000 and based on Santa Cruz Operation's UNIX-based NC operating system, is notebook PC-sized and is designed to replace desktop PCs.

INFOWORLD - In the latest release of its Windows 95 operating system, Microsoft Corp has disabled the dual-boot feature that allowed users to easily switch to Windows 3.1 or other environments, Infoworld reported in its Oct. 14 issue.
Hewlett-Packard Co, Sun Microsystems Inc and International Business Machines Corp's Lotus unit are preparing electronic mail clients using Java code, InfoWorld reported.

INFORMATION WEEK - Tandem Computers Inc plans middleware that will allow users to create cross-platform applications, the latest step to integrate its fault-tolerant technology into multivendor environments, Information Week reported in its Oct. 14 issue.
Guarantees like one offered by American Telephone and Telegraph Co are not enough to turn the Internet into a completely reliable business channel, corporate users told Information Week.

COMMUNICATIONS WEEK - International Business Machines Corp and Sun Microsystems Inc plan to introduce low-cost network terminals later this month, Communications Week reported in its October 14 issue. IBM's Network Station will be built around the PowerPC chip, contain eight megabytes of random access memory and cost $695 for a basic unit. Sun's Mr. Coffee machine will run Java applications only and be designed for fixed uses such as airline reservation systems or retail checkout.

Computer Associates International Inc and IBM planned to make a series of announcements to extend their respective enterprise systems management offerings, Communications Week so said. The two companies are in a race to supply the most complete end-to-end systems management solution, connecting both PCs and mainframes.

COMPUTERWORLD - Delays in upgrading the computer systems of the Internal Revenue Service are depriving the U.S. treasury of as much as $50 billion in uncollected tax revenues per year, Computerworld reported October 14.

ELECTRONIC BUYERS' NEWS - The fortunes of manufacturers of computer memory chip known as Dynamic Random Access Memories (DRAM) are beginning to turn up as PC demand has recovered, pricing has strengthened and inventory supplies have tightened, EBN reported in its October 14 issue. Contract prices have jumped as much as 30 percent for some parts, the magazine said. NEC Corp plans to raise prices 10 to 15 percent in November, for example.
